findings.title: Anonymous readers see favorited/following = true whenever anyone favorited the article or follows the author
Usernames are not unique: PUT /api/user lets any user take an existing username
Saving an article whose slug has a -N suffix changes its slug on every PUT, even with the title unchanged
List filters can't be combined: tag, author and favorited are an else-if chain, so extra filters are silently ignored
A title with no letters or digits gets an empty slug, so the article can't be fetched, edited or deleted
Duplicate and empty tags are stored and returned as given
Email uniqueness and login are case-sensitive, so one mailbox can hold several accounts
Security & Privacy issue (details withheld)
Reachable advisory in the JWT library: golang-jwt/jwt/v5 v5.2.1 allocates ~16x a malformed token's size before rejecting it (CVE-2025-30204)
Session tokens are accepted from the access_token query parameter, and the default access log writes full URLs, tokens included
No rate limiting, lockout or throttling on login
AuthMiddleware treats a validly signed token for a missing user as authenticated, and panics on a token without a numeric id claim
Deleting an article only soft-deletes it: its content, comments and favorites stay in the database with no purge
Database errors are ignored on core read paths and in article creation, so failures come back as 200 with empty or wrong data
No HTTP server timeouts and no request-body size limit
Startup doesn't fail fast: database open and migration errors are printed and ignored until a nil-pointer panic
Favorite and follow are check-then-insert with no unique constraint, so concurrent repeats store duplicates and inflate favoritesCount
Creating an article or comment has no idempotency key or duplicate check, so a client retry after a timeout publishes it twice
No backup or restore path for the SQLite file that holds every account, password hash and article
Multi-step writes are not transactional: article updates commit fields and tags separately, and new tags are inserted before the article
Schema changes rely on AutoMigrate at every startup, with no versioned or reversible migrations
Validators and serializers do database I/O: binding writes rows, and every response serializer runs its own queries
Articles, comments and favorites point at a lazily created ArticleUserModel shadow of each user, created by FirstOrCreate even on GET requests
One package-level *gorm.DB, read through common.GetDB() by every model function, with no injection seam
articles depends on users' internals: it queries the users table directly and reads the user from gin.Context by a string key with unchecked type assertions
common is a junk drawer: JWT minting, random strings, error formatting, request binding, the DB connection and a JSON tri-state type
Test-only helpers live in production files
PUT /api/user skips the validation POST /api/users applies: bio length and image URL are unchecked on update
Error contract is inconsistent across endpoints: raw driver messages under a database key, 404 for DB failures, and a body-less 401
Data-access helpers take interface{} conditions, and GORM silently drops zero-valued fields from them
Operational settings are hard-coded: token lifetime 24 h and the default page size, the latter twice
Three leftover RealWorld template docs at the repo root still say to delete them before publishing
Unused and duplicate code: an unused Database type, a token-extraction helper that duplicates the middleware's, and commented-out code
Non-idiomatic, inconsistent naming from the 2017 code: snake_case identifiers, self receivers, and near-identical exported names
Stale or misleading comments in core and test code
Two complexity hotspots: ArticleUpdate (cyclomatic 19, 80 lines) and FindManyArticle (14, 73 lines)
Copy-paste between paired handlers and in limit/offset parsing
Many tests assert only status codes or key presence, and core behaviors are unpinned: the defects in A1 and A4 all pass the suite
Tests depend on the environment and on each other: a permission-based test fails as root, and table tests share one database in sequence
Article bodies, descriptions and comments are capped at 2048 characters, so a normal-length blog post can't be published
No CORS support: browser frontends on another origin cannot call the API
A password over 72 bytes, which passes the 255-character validation limit, is rejected at registration as 'body is invalid'
The spec-test script silently deletes the default development database
The install steps tell adopters to run go mod tidy, which rewrites go.mod and go.sum
No runnable request examples or container setup for adopters
README says a .env file works with source, but .env.example has no export lines, so the server silently ignores it
README has two coverage tables that disagree with each other and with the code
Stale structure in the README: the directory tree shows gorm.db at the root, and an orphaned 'or' follows the spec-test section
AGENTS.md's lint command fails with a current golangci-lint: the config is in the retired v1 format and CI pins v1.61
CI runs tests through a bespoke per-directory coverage loop instead of the standard go test -coverprofile ./...
No contribution guide, task runner or seed data for local development
No deployment path at all: no container image, release artifact, deploy docs or runbook
Configuration isn't externalized for secrets: only the port, run mode and SQLite paths can be set per environment
Health route answers only at /api/ping/ with a trailing slash, the example config runs in debug mode, and there is no graceful shutdown
The security scan never fails the build: gosec runs with -no-fail
The Bruno CLI used by a CI job is installed unpinned
No structured logs, request IDs or metrics, and handler errors are returned to clients without being logged
GORM's default logger records every expected lookup miss as an error, with the SQL and bound values, so logs are noisy and carry emails
List and comment responses run a following query per item (N+1), and serializing can write rows
No indexes on the foreign keys every request filters by
Page size has no upper bound, and a negative limit disables it
The SQLite driver requires cgo: a CGO_ENABLED=0 build compiles but fails at startup
Toolchain targets are end-of-life: go.mod says go 1.21 and CI tests only Go 1.21-1.23, with dependencies held back to keep them
No automated dependency updates
No release discipline for the API: the last tag is from 2017 and client-visible behavior changes since then have no version or changelog
Concurrency is never exercised by tests: no race detector in CI and no concurrent tests
Dependency licenses are not checked and no SBOM is produced
